title: Collecting Data and Training Models
subject: AI-Literacy
description: How AI models learn from data: training data, labels, models, testing and accuracy; the six steps to train a cloud-spotting AI; planning data collection for a footprint AI; why humans stay involved; the AI Trainer badge; and the skin-checking AI story about what goes wrong when data is missing.

questions.question: In the worksheet's matching exercise, what is 'training data'?
options: The organised examples used to teach an AI
A tag attached to data that names what it is
A check of the AI on brand-new examples
A count of how often the AI answers right
questions.explanation: The worksheet matches Training Data with 'the organised examples used to teach an AI'. The other meanings belong to Label, Testing and Accuracy.

questions.question: Which AI word means 'a tag attached to data that tells the AI what it is'?
options: Model
Label
Testing
Accuracy
questions.explanation: A label is the tag on each piece of data (for example the word 'Cumulus' on a cloud photo) that tells the AI what that data shows.

questions.question: Which AI word means 'checking how well the AI works on new examples it has not seen before'?
options: Training data
Label
Testing
Model
questions.explanation: Testing is done with new, unseen examples so we can see how well the AI really learned, not just whether it remembers the training photos.

questions.question: Which AI word means 'the AI system that has been trained and can now make predictions'?
options: Label
Accuracy
Testing
Model
questions.explanation: The model is the trained AI system. After training, the model can look at a new example and make a prediction about it.

questions.question: Which AI word means 'how often the AI gives the correct answer'?
options: Accuracy
Label
Testing
Model
questions.explanation: Accuracy tells us how often the AI is right. If it gets 9 of 10 new photos right, its accuracy is high.

questions.question: A label is a tag attached to data that tells the AI what that data is.
questions.explanation: This is exactly the worksheet's meaning for 'Label' (meaning E in the matching table).

questions.question: Testing means checking the AI on the same photos that were used to train it.
questions.explanation: Testing uses NEW examples the AI has not seen before. Re-checking the training photos would only show that the AI remembers them, not that it learned.

questions.question: Accuracy tells us how fast an AI gives its answer.
questions.explanation: Accuracy is about how OFTEN the AI gives the correct answer, not about speed.

questions.question: A photo of a cloud has the word 'Cumulus' written beside it so the AI knows what it shows. In AI words, 'Cumulus' here is the ___.
options: testing
label
model
accuracy
questions.explanation: The word attached to the photo that tells the AI what it is called is the label.

questions.question: After the weather station finishes training, the thing that can now look at a sky photo and predict its cloud type is called the ___.
options: category
label
model
dataset
questions.explanation: Once training is done, the trained AI system that makes predictions is the model.

questions.question: 'The AI got 8 out of 10 new photos right.' Which AI word does this sentence describe?
options: Category
Label
Training data
Accuracy
questions.explanation: Counting how often the AI is correct on new photos is its accuracy.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes testing?
options: Showing the AI new photos it never saw to count how many it gets right
Showing the AI its labelled photos again so that it remembers them better
Adding the correct tag to every photo before the training begins
Deciding which cloud categories the AI will be taught to recognise
questions.explanation: Testing uses photos the AI has never seen. Repeating labelled photos is training, adding tags is labelling, and choosing categories is the planning step.

questions.question: Which TWO of these happen BEFORE a trained model exists?
options: Collecting the photos
Labelling the photos
Testing the model on new photos
Recording the model's accuracy
questions.explanation: Photos are collected and labelled first; they become the training data. Testing and measuring accuracy can only happen after a model has been trained.

questions.question: Riya says, 'The model is the big pile of cloud photos we collected.' What is wrong with this?
options: The pile of photos is the test; the model is the accuracy
The pile of photos is training data; the model is the trained AI
Nothing is wrong; the photos and the model are the same thing
The pile of photos is the label; the model is the camera
questions.explanation: The collected photos are the training data. The model is the AI system that is produced after it is trained on those photos.

questions.question: How many AI words did the worksheet's matching exercise ask you to match with meanings?
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation: There were five words: Training Data, Label, Testing, Model and Accuracy, matched with meanings A to E.

questions.question: Which pair is matched CORRECTLY?
options: Label – the trained AI that predicts
Model – a tag attached to the data
Testing – examples used to teach AI
Accuracy – how often the AI is correct
questions.explanation: Only the first pair is right. Label is the tag, Model is the trained AI, and Testing is checking on new examples.

questions.question: Select the TWO correct matches.
options: Training data – organised examples used to teach an AI
Testing – checking the AI on new examples it has not seen
Label – how often the AI gives the correct answer
Model – a tag attached to data saying what it is
questions.explanation: The first two are correct. The third describes accuracy (not label) and the fourth describes a label (not a model).

questions.question: Why should the testing photos be DIFFERENT from the training photos?
options: So we see if the AI really learned, not just remembered
So the AI has more photos to memorise before the test
So the photos can be labelled a second time by a human
So the model becomes larger and takes longer to train
questions.explanation: If the AI is tested on photos it already saw, a good score could just be memory. New photos show whether it truly learned the pattern.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: A weather station is training an AI to identify cloud types. What is the FIRST step in the correct sequence?
options: Test the model on new cloud photos it has not seen
Decide what categories to use, such as Cumulus and Stratus
Photograph hundreds of clouds on sunny and stormy days
Label each photo with the correct cloud type
questions.explanation: You must decide the categories (Cumulus, Stratus, Cirrus, Nimbus) first, so you know what you are collecting and what labels to use.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: What is the LAST (sixth) step in the cloud AI sequence?
options: Feed all the labelled photos into the AI tool
Decide which four cloud categories to use
If accuracy is low, collect more photos and retrain
Label each photo with careful human checking
questions.explanation: After testing, the final step is to collect more photos and retrain if accuracy is low — especially for the categories the AI keeps getting wrong.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which step comes right AFTER photographing hundreds of clouds?
options: Retraining the model with even more photos
Deciding which categories the AI should learn
Testing the model on new cloud photos
Labelling each photo with its correct cloud type
questions.explanation: Order: decide categories → photograph clouds → label each photo → train → test → retrain if needed. Labelling follows photographing.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which step comes right AFTER labelling the photos?
options: Feeding the labelled photos into the AI tool
Recording how many test photos it got right
Deciding the categories to use
Photographing more stormy clouds
questions.explanation: Once photos are labelled, they are fed into the AI tool to train the model. Testing comes after that.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which step comes right AFTER feeding the labelled photos into the AI tool to train the model?
options: Photograph the same clouds again from a different angle
Test the model on new photos and record how many it gets right
Decide what the four cloud categories should be called
Label every photo again to be sure no mistakes were made
questions.explanation: Training is step 4. Step 5 is testing the model on new cloud photos it has never seen and recording how many it gets right.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which four cloud categories did the weather station decide to use?
options: Cirrus, Nimbus, Thunder, Mist
Stratus, Cirrus, Sunny, Rainy
Cumulus, Stratus, Cirrus, Nimbus
Cumulus, Stratus, Fog, Rainbow
questions.explanation: The worksheet lists Cumulus, Stratus, Cirrus and Nimbus as example categories.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Why did the station photograph clouds on sunny days, rainy days AND stormy days?
options: So the camera battery is used up evenly every week
So the photos can be sorted by the day of the week
So the AI learns to predict tomorrow's temperature
So the AI sees clouds in many conditions, not just one
questions.explanation: Variety in the training photos helps the AI recognise clouds in all kinds of weather, not only the conditions it happened to see.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: The worksheet says labelling each photo with the correct cloud type takes careful human checking.
questions.explanation: Step D says exactly this: labelling 'takes careful human checking'.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: The weather station should test the model BEFORE labelling the photos.
questions.explanation: There is no model to test until the labelled photos have been used for training. Testing comes after training.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: If accuracy is low, the station should collect more photos, especially of the cloud types the AI keeps getting wrong, and retrain.
questions.explanation: This is step F, the last step in the sequence.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: In the correct six-step order, which action is step 4?
options: Feeding labelled photos into the AI tool
Deciding the cloud categories
Photographing hundreds of clouds
Testing on new cloud photos
questions.explanation: Steps: 1 decide categories, 2 photograph, 3 label, 4 feed photos to train, 5 test, 6 retrain if needed.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: In the correct six-step order, which action is step 2?
options: Test the model and record the results
Photograph hundreds of different clouds
Collect more photos and retrain the model
Label each photo with the correct type
questions.explanation: After deciding categories (step 1), the station photographs hundreds of clouds (step 2).

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Why does the worksheet say to photograph HUNDREDS of clouds rather than just a few?
options: Hundreds of photos make the camera focus more sharply
The weather station must fill its memory card first
Many examples help the AI learn the pattern of each type
A few photos would make the AI tool refuse to start
questions.explanation: An AI learns from examples. More varied examples of each category help it learn what that category really looks like.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: After testing, the model gets most Nimbus photos wrong but the other types right. According to the worksheet, what should the station do?
options: Remove Nimbus so the accuracy score looks higher
Test the model again on exactly the same photos
Relabel the Cumulus photos as Nimbus to balance
Collect more Nimbus photos and retrain the model
questions.explanation: Step F says: if accuracy is low, collect more photos and retrain, especially for the categories the AI keeps getting wrong.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Why can't the station label the photos BEFORE deciding the categories?
options: Without categories, nobody knows which tags to write
Labels can only be added after the model is tested
The camera adds the labels while taking photos
Photos must be fed to the AI tool before labelling
questions.explanation: A label is the category name on a photo. You have to decide the categories first to know what labels exist.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which TWO steps clearly need careful human judgement?
options: Labelling each photo with the right cloud type
Deciding which cloud categories to use
The AI tool finding patterns during training
The model giving its prediction for a test photo
questions.explanation: Humans decide the categories and check every label. Finding patterns and making predictions are what the AI tool and model do.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: How many steps are there in the cloud AI sequence on the worksheet?
options: Five
Six
Seven
Four
questions.explanation: The steps are lettered A to F and must be numbered 1 to 6.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Which of these is the TESTING step?
options: Write the correct cloud type on every photograph
Choose Cumulus, Stratus, Cirrus and Nimbus as types
Show the model new photos and count how many it gets right
Feed all the labelled photos into the AI tool at once
questions.explanation: Testing means showing the model new photos it has never seen and recording how many it gets right.

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: The steps are: A photograph, B test, C decide categories, D label, E feed to train, F retrain if low. Which order is correct?
options: A, C, D, E, B, F
C, A, E, D, B, F
C, D, A, E, F, B
C, A, D, E, B, F
questions.explanation: Decide (C) → photograph (A) → label (D) → train (E) → test (B) → retrain if accuracy is low (F).

questions.topic: Training a Cloud AI: Six Steps in Order
questions.question: Once the cloud model has been retrained a single time, it will never need more photos again.
questions.explanation: Step F is a loop: whenever accuracy is low, collect more photos and retrain. It may be needed more than once.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: What did the nature club want to train an AI to identify?
options: Animal footprints from photos
Bird songs from recordings
Tree types from leaf shapes
Cloud types from the sky
questions.explanation: The nature club wants an AI that identifies animal footprints from photos.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Why did the nature club want a footprint-identifying AI?
options: To find out which animals are the fastest
To learn which animals visit the forest at night
To count how many trees grow in the forest
To predict the weather in the forest each day
questions.explanation: The club wants to learn which animals visit the forest at night, when nobody is there to see them.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: How many animals (categories) does the planning board ask the AI to learn?
options: Five
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation: The planning board has Category 1, Category 2 and Category 3 — three animals.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: The planning board offers 5, 50 or 500 photos per animal. Which choice gives the AI the BEST chance to learn each footprint well?
options: 50 photos
5 photos
Any number is equal
500 photos
questions.explanation: An AI learns from examples, and footprints vary with the ground and light. More photos (500) give the AI far more to learn from than 5 or 50.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Why would collecting only 5 photos per animal be a poor choice?
options: Too few examples to learn how each footprint can vary
Five photos take too long for a person to label
The AI tool cannot open fewer than fifty photos
Five photos would make the test score too high
questions.explanation: With only 5 photos, the AI sees very little variety and may not recognise the same footprint in different mud, sand or light.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Which set of three conditions would give the footprint photos GOOD variety?
options: The same spot on three sunny days
Wet mud, dry sand and soft snow
Dry sand at noon, three times over
One deer print copied three times
questions.explanation: Variety means different ground, weather and light. Mud, sand and snow show the same footprint in three different conditions.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Select the TWO conditions that add useful VARIETY to the footprint photos.
options: Footprints in mud and footprints in sand
Footprints in bright daylight and in dim light
Footprints photographed from one fixed angle only
Footprints of only one animal, the deer
questions.explanation: Different ground and different light are real variety. One fixed angle and one animal only reduce variety.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Which of these is something that could go WRONG with the club's data collection?
options: Photos are taken in mud, sand and snow
The club decides to collect 500 photos
Some photos get labelled with the wrong animal
The club chooses three different animals
questions.explanation: Wrong labels teach the AI the wrong thing. Choosing three animals, varied ground and many photos are good planning, not problems.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Some footprint photos were labelled with the wrong animal. What is the best way to FIX this?
options: Train the model anyway and hope it ignores them
Delete all the photos and give up on the project
Rename every photo with the first animal's name
Have a person carefully check and correct the labels
questions.explanation: Labelling needs careful human checking. Correcting the wrong labels fixes the problem before the AI learns from them.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: The club collects 500 photos of deer prints but only 5 of fox prints. What is the likely problem?
options: The AI learns deer well but often misses fox
The AI will learn fox better because it is rarer
The AI cannot start until both have 500 photos
There is no problem since 505 is a large number
questions.explanation: An AI learns exactly what it is shown. With far fewer fox examples, it will recognise fox prints much less reliably — like the skin-checking AI story.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: The planning board asks for three different conditions the footprints should appear in.
questions.explanation: The board says: 'List 3 different conditions the footprints should appear in'.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: If many of the club's footprint photos are blurry, the AI may learn the wrong pattern.
questions.explanation: The AI learns from what it is shown. Blurry photos are poor data and can lead to poor learning.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Which planning choice would give the footprint AI the WEAKEST training?
options: 500 photos per animal in day and night light
5 photos per animal, all taken at one spot
500 photos per animal, taken in many places
50 photos per animal in mud, sand and snow
questions.explanation: Few photos and no variety is the weakest mix: the AI sees too little to learn how each footprint can look.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Why should the footprint photos be taken in different conditions?
options: Animals only leave prints when the weather changes
The AI tool refuses photos that all look similar
Forest ground and light change, so prints look different
The camera needs practice in many kinds of weather
questions.explanation: The AI must recognise a footprint wherever it appears, so it should see examples in mud, sand, wet and dry, light and dark.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: The club notices it has very few photos of one animal. Which fix matches the chapter's advice?
options: Remove that animal from the project quietly
Copy one photo many times to make it 500
Label other animals' prints with that animal
Collect more photos of that animal and retrain
questions.explanation: The chapter's rule is to collect more photos for categories the AI gets wrong and retrain. Copies and false labels do not add real variety.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Select the TWO things that could go WRONG in the club's data collection.
options: Some photos are labelled with the wrong animal
Photos were taken in rain, sand and mud
Only a few photos of one animal were collected
The club chose three different animals to study
questions.explanation: Wrong labels and too few photos of one animal are real problems. Varied conditions and three categories are part of a good plan.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: At what time do the animals the club is interested in visit the forest?
options: At night
At noon
At dawn only
At the weekend
questions.explanation: The club wants to learn which animals visit the forest at night.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: Choosing 500 photos per animal means the club no longer needs any variety in the photos.
questions.explanation: Quantity and variety are both needed. 500 near-identical photos would still leave the AI unprepared for different ground or light.

questions.topic: Planning the Footprint AI: Data Collection
questions.question: The club trains its AI on deer, rabbit and dog prints. Later it is shown a cat print. What will the AI most likely do?
options: Teach itself about cats by looking at the photo
Guess one of its three animals, since that is all it learned
Correctly say 'cat' because it is a smart computer
Refuse to answer and ask the club for a new category
questions.explanation: The AI learned exactly what it was shown — three animals. It cannot know about a category it never saw, so it will pick one of the three.

questions.question: Which step did the worksheet say 'takes careful human checking'?
options: The model predicting a type for a new photo
The camera taking hundreds of cloud photos
Labelling each photo with the correct cloud type
Feeding the photos into the AI tool to train it
questions.explanation: Step D, labelling, is the one that 'takes careful human checking'.

questions.question: Why are humans needed at the LABELLING step?
options: Labels can only be typed on a human's keyboard
The AI tool charges money for each unlabelled photo
Humans are faster than computers at sorting photos
The AI does not know what a photo shows until it is told
questions.explanation: The AI learns from labels. A human must say 'this is Cirrus' for the AI to learn what Cirrus looks like.

questions.question: Why are humans needed at the TESTING step?
options: To record the results and judge if accuracy is good enough
To take the test instead of the AI if it feels tired
To add new labels to the photos during the test
To make the model run faster on the new photos
questions.explanation: Humans show new photos, record how many the model gets right, and decide whether accuracy is high enough or more data is needed.

questions.question: Why are humans needed when deciding the CATEGORIES?
options: Categories must be written by hand on every photo
Only people know what the project needs the AI to recognise
Computers cannot store more than four categories at once
The AI can choose categories but prefers to be told
questions.explanation: The weather station or nature club decides what matters to them — cloud types or three animals. The AI cannot know the project's purpose.

questions.question: Select TWO reasons humans are still needed when training an AI model.
options: To decide which categories the AI should learn
To check that every label is correct
To make the computer's processor run faster
To take over all predictions once training ends
questions.explanation: Humans choose the categories and check labels. Humans do not speed up the processor, and the model (not humans) makes predictions after training.

questions.question: Once an AI model is trained, humans no longer need to check its results.
questions.explanation: Testing and retraining both depend on humans checking results. The badge rule 'always check the results' says the same.

questions.question: Humans decide when accuracy is low and more photos are needed.
questions.explanation: Step F — collect more photos and retrain if accuracy is low — is a human decision made after looking at the test results.

questions.question: Which statement about humans and AI training is correct?
options: Humans are needed only once, at the very end, to approve the model
Humans only take the photos; the AI labels, trains and tests itself
The AI learns only what humans show it, so humans must choose data carefully
The AI learns everything by itself, so humans only switch it on
questions.explanation: The chapter's key idea: the AI learned exactly what it was shown. Humans choose, label and check the data at every step.

questions.question: What do learners in the school's 'AI Training Club' do?
options: Build robots and race them around the school
Write the AI's code and repair the computers
Only watch videos about how AI tools work
Collect photos, organise data and check labels
questions.explanation: The worksheet says club learners help collect photos, organise data, and check labels so simple AI tools can learn correctly.

questions.question: The skin-checking AI 'wasn't broken'. So what actually needed to change?
options: The data the humans had chosen to train it with
The computer the AI program was running on
The number of scientists working on the AI
The camera used to take the medical photos
questions.explanation: The AI did what it was taught. The dataset lacked darker-skin photos, so the humans needed to collect better, more complete data.

questions.question: If humans label photos carelessly, the AI will still learn the right answer because it is smart.
questions.explanation: The AI learns exactly what it is shown. Careless labels teach it the wrong thing, which is why labelling needs careful human checking.

questions.question: Who notices that the model keeps getting one category wrong?
options: The AI tool while it is still being trained
The humans who test it and record the results
The model itself, which then fixes its mistakes
The camera that took the original photos
questions.explanation: Testing and recording results is a human step. That is how people learn which categories need more photos.

questions.question: Which is the best short answer to 'Why do humans still need to be involved at different steps?'
options: People are needed only to buy the camera and the AI software
People must write every prediction the model will ever make
People must decide, label, test and fix; the AI only learns what it is given
People must stay nearby in case the computer needs to be switched off
questions.explanation: Humans decide categories, label carefully, test responsibly and retrain when needed, because the AI learns exactly what it is shown.

questions.question: Humans are needed both at the start (choosing categories) and at the end (checking accuracy), not just at one step.
questions.explanation: The worksheet asks why humans are needed 'at different steps' — from planning through labelling to testing and retraining.

questions.question: Which TWO things can the cloud AI NOT do by itself?
options: Decide that Nimbus is a category worth learning
Notice its answers are wrong and go photograph more clouds
Find patterns in the labelled photos it is given
Give a prediction for a brand-new sky photo
questions.explanation: Choosing categories and deciding to collect more data are human steps. Finding patterns and predicting are what the trained model does.

questions.question: A learner says, 'Let the AI label the footprint photos itself, it will be quicker.' What is the problem?
options: The AI can label but only in capital letters
Labels made by an AI are always too long to read
The AI would need 500 photos just to type one label
Before training, the AI does not yet know which print is which
questions.explanation: Labels are how the AI learns in the first place. An untrained AI cannot know a deer print from a fox print.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: According to the teacher, what THREE things earn the 'AI Trainer' badge?
options: Collect good data, label carefully, test responsibly
Build a robot, write code, win a competition
Take photos, print them, stick them on a wall
Buy a camera, buy software, buy a computer
questions.explanation: The badge is for anyone who understands how to collect good data, label it carefully, and test the AI responsibly.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which badge titles did the worksheet give as examples?
options: Label Master and Test Pilot
AI Trainer and Data Detective
Robot Boss and Code King
Cloud Spotter and Print Finder
questions.explanation: The worksheet suggests 'AI Trainer, Data Detective, or your own idea'.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: How many things must the AI Trainer badge include?
options: Four: a title, a photo, a rule and a date
One: just a title for the club
Three: a title, a symbol and a rule
Two: a title and a colour
questions.explanation: The badge must include a title, one symbol that represents data or AI learning, and one rule about training AI responsibly.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which example rules did the worksheet suggest for the badge?
options: 'Train fast' or 'Never test twice'
'Trust the AI' or 'Skip the labels'
'Use five photos' or 'Keep it secret'
'Use clear labels' or 'Always check the results'
questions.explanation: The worksheet's examples are 'Use clear labels' and 'always check the results'.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which rule would best fit on a responsible AI Trainer badge?
options: Always check the results
Trust the AI's first answer
Label photos as fast as you can
Test only when you have time
questions.explanation: Checking results is one of the worksheet's own example rules. The other options skip the careful checking the chapter asks for.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: The badge must include one symbol that represents data or AI learning.
questions.explanation: This is one of the three required parts of the badge design.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Why is 'Use clear labels' a RESPONSIBLE training rule?
options: Clear labels make the model train in less than a minute
The AI learns from labels, so unclear ones teach it wrong things
Clear labels make the photos look neater on the wall
The AI tool only accepts labels written in clear ink
questions.explanation: Labels are what the AI learns from. If labels are unclear or wrong, the model learns the wrong pattern.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Why is 'Always check the results' a RESPONSIBLE training rule?
options: Checking results makes the AI train on fewer photos
The AI stops working if nobody looks at its answers
The AI can be wrong, and only testing shows where it fails
Results must be checked so the badge can be printed
questions.explanation: The skin-checking story shows an AI can look fine yet fail for some people. Checking results is how humans catch that.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which of these would NOT be a responsible training rule?
options: Check who might be missing from the data
Label every photo carefully and clearly
Test the model on photos it has not seen
Use as few photos as possible to save time
questions.explanation: Few photos mean little variety and poor learning. The other three match the chapter's advice.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Select the TWO rules that show responsible AI training.
options: Use clear labels
Always check the results
Skip testing if training took a long time
Use only photos the AI finds easy
questions.explanation: The first two are the worksheet's own examples. Skipping tests and using only easy photos would hide the AI's mistakes.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: The AI Training Club helps simple AI tools learn ___.
options: correctly
quickly
secretly
loudly
questions.explanation: The worksheet says learners check labels 'so that simple AI tools can learn correctly'.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: A learner writes the badge rule 'Check who and what might be missing from the data.' Which part of the chapter does this echo?
options: The meaning of 'model' in the matching exercise
The scientists' advice after the skin-checking AI story
The list of four cloud categories in the weather project
The choice between 5, 50 and 500 footprint photos
questions.explanation: The scientists said: 'Before training an AI, always check who — and what — might be missing from the data.'

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which badge rule would have helped PREVENT the skin-checking AI problem?
options: Test the AI on the photos it was trained with
Use the biggest computer available for training
Include photos of everyone the AI will be used for
Train the AI on the clearest photos only
questions.explanation: The AI failed on darker skin because such photos were missing. Including everyone the AI will serve is the fix the scientists recommend.

questions.topic: The AI Trainer Badge: Responsible Training Rules
questions.question: Which badge design meets ALL the worksheet's requirements?
options: Title 'Data Detective', a magnifying-glass symbol, and the club's meeting time
A photo of the teacher, the school's name, and the rule 'Have fun'
Title 'AI Trainer', the date of the first meeting, and a gold border
Title 'Data Detective', a magnifying-glass-over-photos symbol, rule 'Use clear labels'
questions.explanation: Only the first has a title, a symbol about data or AI learning, AND a responsible-training rule.

questions.question: What were the scientists' AI trained to do?
options: Spot signs of skin disease from photos
Identify cloud types from sky photos
Recognise animal footprints in the forest
Read handwriting on medical forms
questions.explanation: The story says scientists trained an AI to spot signs of skin disease from photos.

questions.question: On which skin did the AI work very well?
options: Neither type
Light skin
Darker skin
All skin equally
questions.explanation: The AI worked very well on light skin but missed more cases on darker skin.

questions.question: What happened when the AI looked at photos of darker skin?
options: It refused to give any answer at all
It gave exactly the same results
It missed more cases of skin disease
It worked better than on light skin
questions.explanation: The AI 'missed more cases on darker skin'.

questions.question: According to the story, was the AI broken?
options: Yes — its program had an error that was later fixed
Yes — its camera could not see darker colours
No — the doctors were using it in the wrong way
No — it learned from a dataset that was unbalanced
questions.explanation: The story says 'The AI wasn't broken.' It simply learned from a dataset with many light-skin photos and far fewer darker-skin photos.

questions.question: WHY did the AI miss more cases on darker skin?
options: Its dataset had many light-skin photos and few darker-skin photos
Darker skin has no visible signs of skin disease to spot
The scientists told the AI to ignore darker-skin photos
The AI was tested before it had finished training
questions.explanation: The AI learned exactly what it was shown. It saw far fewer examples of darker skin, so it learned those cases less well.

questions.question: What do scientists now say should be done BEFORE training an AI?
options: Decide how many people will use the finished AI
Check who and what might be missing from the data
Buy the fastest computer that money can afford
Test the AI on the photos it will be trained with
questions.explanation: The story ends: 'Before training an AI, always check who — and what — might be missing from the data.'

questions.question: The skin-checking AI worked equally well for everyone.
questions.explanation: The title itself says it 'worked great for some people — but NOT for everyone'. It missed more cases on darker skin.

questions.question: The story says the AI learned exactly what it was shown.
questions.explanation: This is a direct line from the story and the key idea of the chapter.

questions.question: The dataset had far fewer photos of darker skin than of light skin.
questions.explanation: The story says the dataset 'had many photos of light skin and far fewer photos of darker skin'.

questions.question: Which fix would help the skin-checking AI the MOST?
options: Tell users with darker skin not to use the AI
Remove the light-skin photos so the dataset is smaller
Add many more darker-skin photos and retrain the model
Test the model again on the light-skin photos it knows
questions.explanation: Collect more photos for the group the AI gets wrong and retrain — the same step-F idea from the cloud sequence.

questions.question: The story's title says the AI worked great for some people 'but NOT for everyone'. Who was left out?
options: People with light skin
People who were scientists
People with no skin disease
People with darker skin
questions.explanation: The AI missed more cases on darker skin, so people with darker skin were not served as well.

questions.question: What does 'The AI learned exactly what it was shown' mean?
options: It could only recognise well what appeared often in its training photos
It memorised every photo and could repeat them back perfectly
It understood skin disease the same way a human doctor does
It learned new things on its own after training finished
questions.explanation: The AI's knowledge comes only from its data. Groups with few examples are learned poorly — nothing extra is 'understood'.

questions.question: WHEN should people check who and what might be missing from the data?
options: Never — the AI checks itself
Before training the AI
Only after people complain
Only once the AI is sold
questions.explanation: The scientists' advice is to check 'before training an AI'.

questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are TRUE about the skin-checking AI story.
options: The AI worked very well on light skin
The AI missed more cases on darker skin
The AI was broken and had to be rebuilt
The dataset had equal photos of all skin tones
questions.explanation: The first two come straight from the story. The AI was not broken, and the dataset was unbalanced, not equal.

questions.question: Who trained the skin-checking AI in the story?
options: A weather station
School learners
Scientists
A nature club
questions.explanation: The story begins: 'Scientists trained an AI to spot signs of skin disease from photos.'

questions.question: At which step of the cloud-AI sequence did the skin-checking project's mistake really happen?
options: Deciding the categories — skin disease was a bad choice
Feeding photos into the AI tool — it was too slow
Testing — the scientists forgot to count results
Collecting the photos — there was too little variety
questions.explanation: The dataset had far fewer darker-skin photos. The problem was in what was collected, not in the categories, the tool or the counting.

questions.question: What kind of photos did the training dataset have MANY of?
options: Photos of light skin
Photos of darker skin
Photos of clouds
Photos of footprints
questions.explanation: The dataset 'had many photos of light skin and far fewer photos of darker skin'.

questions.question: In the skin-checking story, what was 'missing from the data'?
options: Photos taken by scientists
Enough photos of darker skin
Enough photos of light skin
Photos of healthy skin only
questions.explanation: The dataset had far fewer photos of darker skin, so that group was effectively missing.

questions.question: Why was the skin-checking AI UNFAIR?
options: It only worked for people who were scientists
It gave slower answers to people in hospitals
How well it helped you depended on your skin tone
It charged some people more money than others
questions.explanation: The AI worked well for light skin and missed more cases on darker skin — its help was unequal.

questions.question: A voice assistant is trained mostly on adult voices. Using the chapter's idea, what is most likely?
options: It works equally well for everyone
It works best for children's voices
It stops working for adults later
It works worse for children's voices
questions.explanation: An AI learns exactly what it is shown. A group with few examples — children — will be recognised less well, like darker skin in the story.

questions.question: The footprint AI is trained only on prints in dry sand. What is the likely result?
options: It often misses prints in mud or snow
It recognises mud prints best of all
It works perfectly on every surface
It refuses to look at sand prints
questions.explanation: Conditions that were missing from the training data are the ones the AI handles worst.

questions.question: An AI with high accuracy on its test photos is guaranteed to work well for every group of people.
questions.explanation: The skin-checking AI may have scored well overall yet failed for darker skin. If a group is missing from the data, the test may not reveal it.

questions.question: Checking who and what might be missing from the data helps make an AI fairer.
questions.explanation: That is exactly why the scientists give this advice — so no group is left out as darker skin was.

questions.question: Which question should a careful data collector ask BEFORE training?
options: Which computer will train the model fastest?
Who or what might be missing from my photos?
Which photo is the prettiest in my collection?
How quickly can I finish labelling all of these?
questions.explanation: This is the scientists' advice from the story.

questions.question: Select the TWO actions that would help AVOID the skin-checking AI's problem.
options: Collect photos from many different kinds of people
Check which groups have few photos before training
Train for longer on the same unbalanced photos
Test only on the photos used for training
questions.explanation: Variety and a 'who is missing' check fix the cause. Longer training on the same data, or testing on training photos, would hide the problem.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: The fewer examples of a group the AI sees, the ___ it learns that group.
options: faster
fairer
worse
better
questions.explanation: The AI learned darker skin poorly because it saw far fewer examples of it.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a lesson from the skin-checking AI story?
options: An AI learns exactly what it is shown
Missing data can make an AI fail for some people
Check who is missing from the data before training
An AI can learn things that humans never showed it
questions.explanation: The story teaches the opposite: the AI learned only from what it was shown, which is why missing data mattered.

questions.question: An AI can only learn from the photos it is given.
questions.explanation: This is the chapter's core idea: the AI learned exactly what it was shown.

questions.question: The weather station photographs clouds only on sunny days. Using the chapter's idea, what will the model likely struggle with?
options: Clouds on stormy or rainy days
Clouds on bright sunny days
Clouds photographed at midday
Clouds in the Cumulus category
questions.explanation: Stormy and rainy conditions would be missing from the data — the 'what' in 'who and what might be missing'.

questions.question: AI-1 was trained on 1000 photos all of one kind of person. AI-2 was trained on 400 photos of many different people. Which is more likely to work fairly for everyone?
options: Neither, because 1000 photos is too few
AI-2, because its data covers more people
AI-1, because 1000 is more than 400
Both the same, since both have hundreds
questions.explanation: Variety matters, not just quantity. AI-1 is like the skin-checking AI — lots of data, but a whole group missing.

questions.question: Adding more photos always fixes unfairness, even if the new photos are all of the same group.
questions.explanation: More photos of the already well-covered group do nothing for the group that is missing. The new photos must fill the gap.

questions.question: Complete the scientists' saying: 'Before training an AI, always ___.'
options: pick the largest number of categories you can
ask the AI which photos it would like to see
check who and what might be missing from the data
test the model on the photos it was trained with
questions.explanation: This is the closing line of the story.

questions.question: Select the TWO signs that a dataset may be missing something important.
options: One category has far fewer photos than the others
All the photos were taken in a single condition
Every photo has been labelled carefully
The photos came from many different places
questions.explanation: Few photos of one category and no variety in conditions are warning signs. Careful labels and many places are good signs.

questions.question: The nature club's AI works well for deer and rabbit but badly for fox. Following the scientists' advice, what should the club check FIRST?
options: Whether the fox is simply too clever to be detected
Whether the computer needs a newer operating system
Whether deer and rabbit photos should be deleted
Whether fox photos were few or missing from the data
questions.explanation: Poor results for one group usually mean that group was under-represented in the data — the skin-checking lesson applied to footprints.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: What big question does the worksheet open with?
options: How might the way data is collected and organised influence what an AI learns?
How might the speed of a computer influence how quickly an AI can learn?
How might the number of scientists on a team influence how smart an AI is?
How might the colour of a camera influence the photos an AI can take?
questions.explanation: The chapter's guiding question is about how data collection and organisation shape what an AI learns.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Why organise the training data into clear categories with labels?
options: So the humans do not have to look at the photos
So every example clearly tells the AI what it shows
So the photos take up less space on the computer
So the AI can skip the training step completely
questions.explanation: Organised, labelled examples are what the worksheet calls training data — the AI learns from each photo's label.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Some Cirrus photos were accidentally labelled 'Stratus'. What will the model most likely learn?
options: That Stratus clouds only appear on stormy days
To correct the labels itself during training
A mixed-up idea of what Stratus and Cirrus look like
Nothing different, since the AI ignores the labels
questions.explanation: The AI learns exactly what it is shown. Wrong labels teach it a wrong pattern.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Which sentence best sums up the chapter's main idea?
options: A bigger computer always produces a smarter AI model
An AI learns the same things no matter what it is shown
Labels are optional once the AI has seen a few photos
The data humans collect and organise decides what the AI knows
questions.explanation: From the cloud steps to the skin-checking story, the message is that an AI learns exactly what its data shows it.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: The way data is collected can change what an AI learns.
questions.explanation: This is the worksheet's guiding question and the lesson of the skin-checking story.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: An AI can learn to recognise a cloud type it has never seen a single photo of.
questions.explanation: The AI learns only from what it is shown. A category with no photos cannot be learned.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: In this chapter, what does 'organised' data mean?
options: Examples sorted into categories, each with a label
Photos arranged from the largest to the smallest file
Photos stored in alphabetical order by file name
Examples that have been tested by the model already
questions.explanation: Training data is 'the organised examples used to teach an AI' — sorted into categories and labelled.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Select the TWO things about the data that strongly influence what the AI learns.
options: Whether each photo has the correct label
Whether every category has enough varied photos
The font used to write the labels
The brand of camera used for the photos
questions.explanation: Correct labels and enough variety per category are what the chapter stresses. Font and camera brand are not what shapes learning.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: The club trained its footprint AI with photos taken only at noon. It is shown a photo taken at dawn. Why might it get this wrong?
options: The AI only works on photos taken by the club
Dawn light looks different from anything it was shown
AI models are switched off early in the morning
Footprints disappear completely before noon
questions.explanation: A condition missing from the data (dawn light) is a condition the AI handles poorly.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Complete: If the training data is poor or unbalanced, the model will be ___.
options: smaller
fairer
unreliable
faster
questions.explanation: The skin-checking AI shows that poor data produces a model that fails for some people.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: A model's accuracy depends partly on the quality of the data used to train it.
questions.explanation: Good, varied, correctly labelled data leads to better accuracy; the footprint and skin examples both show this.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Which TWO steps of the cloud sequence are about ORGANISING the data?
options: Photographing clouds and testing the model
Training the model and retraining it later
Testing the model and recording the results
Deciding categories and labelling the photos
questions.explanation: Choosing categories and labelling sort the photos into organised training data.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Match the action to its name: taking photos is 'collecting'; which action is 'organising'?
options: Labelling photos into their categories
Feeding photos into the AI tool
Counting how many test photos were right
Choosing the biggest computer available
questions.explanation: Collecting gathers examples; organising sorts and labels them; training feeds them to the AI; testing checks the model.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: What kind of data was collected in BOTH the cloud project and the footprint project?
options: Written stories
Photos
Sound recordings
Temperature readings
questions.explanation: The weather station photographs clouds and the nature club photographs footprints.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are TRUE about data and AI.
options: An AI learns exactly what it is shown
Low accuracy can be improved by collecting more photos and retraining
An AI understands what a cloud is without any labelled photos
Testing should be done on the same photos used for training
questions.explanation: The first two come from the story and step F. The others contradict the chapter: labels are needed, and testing uses new photos.

questions.topic: How Data Shapes What AI Learns
questions.question: Two clubs train footprint AIs. Club A labels carefully and photographs in many conditions; Club B labels in a hurry and uses one spot. Whose model will most likely be better?
options: Both equally
Impossible to say
Club A's
Club B's
questions.explanation: Careful labels and varied data are what the chapter says lead to a model that learns correctly.

questions.question: What should be recorded during the testing step?
options: How many photos were labelled by each person
How long the camera took to photograph clouds
How many categories the station first decided
How many new photos the model gets right
questions.explanation: Step B: test the model on new photos 'and record how many it gets right'.

questions.question: The model gets 3 out of 10 new photos right. According to the worksheet, what should happen next?
options: Collect more photos and retrain the model
Declare the model finished and start using it
Test again on the same 10 photos to be sure
Reduce the categories from four to one
questions.explanation: 3 of 10 is low accuracy, so step F applies: collect more photos and retrain.

questions.question: What should the station do if accuracy is low?
options: Relabel photos to match the model's guesses
Collect more photos and retrain
Delete the model and stop the project
Use the model anyway for forecasts
questions.explanation: This is step F of the sequence.

questions.question: When collecting more photos after a low score, which categories should get special attention?
options: The ones with the most photos already
The ones with the shortest names
The ones the AI keeps getting wrong
The ones the AI already gets right
questions.explanation: Step F says: 'especially for categories the AI keeps getting wrong'.

questions.question: Accuracy is measured using photos the model has never seen before.
questions.explanation: Testing on new photos is how we measure how often the model is correct.

questions.question: If accuracy is low, the best fix is to test the model again on the same photos.
questions.explanation: Retesting on the same photos changes nothing. The worksheet's fix is to collect more photos and retrain.

questions.question: A model gets 20 of 20 training photos right but only 8 of 20 NEW photos right. What should we conclude?
options: Its accuracy is perfect because 20 of 20 is 100 percent
The new photos must be faulty since the model knows clouds
The model should only ever be used on its training photos
Its real accuracy is low; it needs more data and retraining
questions.explanation: Only the result on NEW photos counts as testing. 8 of 20 is low, so step F applies.

questions.question: Why is it important to RECORD the test results?
options: To know whether more photos and retraining are needed
To prove to the camera that the photos were used
To make the model train faster the next time
To decide which cloud is the prettiest of all
questions.explanation: The recorded results show whether accuracy is high enough or whether step F (retrain) is needed.

questions.question: Select the TWO things to do after a LOW test score.
options: Collect more photos, especially of the weak categories
Retrain the model with the new photos
Stop testing so the low score is not recorded
Use the model for real work straight away
questions.explanation: Step F: collect more photos and retrain. Hiding the score or using a weak model would be irresponsible.

questions.question: Accuracy is described in the worksheet as ___.
options: how many categories the AI can store
how often the AI gives the correct answer
how many photos were used in training
how quickly the AI tool finishes training
questions.explanation: This is the worksheet's meaning for 'Accuracy' (meaning C).

questions.question: A model with low accuracy should be used anyway, because retraining takes too much time.
questions.explanation: The responsible step is to collect more photos and retrain. Using a weak model could give many wrong answers.

questions.question: The model gets Cumulus, Stratus and Cirrus right most of the time but Nimbus wrong most of the time. What is the best plan?
options: Drop Nimbus from the list of categories
Test only on Cumulus, Stratus and Cirrus
Collect more Nimbus photos and retrain
Collect more Cumulus photos and retrain
questions.explanation: Focus new photos on the category the AI keeps getting wrong, then retrain — exactly step F.

questions.question: Why does testing happen AFTER training and not before?
options: Testing before training makes the photos blurry
The worksheet says testing is optional at the start
Humans are too busy labelling to test earlier
There is no trained model to test until training is done
questions.explanation: A model only exists after the labelled photos are used to train it; testing checks that model.

questions.question: Retraining means training the model again with more or better photos.
questions.explanation: Step F: collect more photos and retrain.

questions.question: What is the best way to know whether the footprint model is ready to use?
options: Test it on new footprint photos and check how many it gets right
Ask the model itself whether it feels ready for the forest
Count how many photos were fed in; 500 means it is ready
Check that every photo in the training set has a label
questions.explanation: Readiness is shown by accuracy on new, unseen photos — not by the amount of training data or the model's own 'opinion'.

questions.question: 'The AI gave the correct answer 90 times out of 100 new photos.' What does this tell us?
options: It was never tested
Its accuracy is high
Its accuracy is low
It needs 10 more labels
questions.explanation: 90 correct out of 100 means the AI is right most of the time — high accuracy.

questions.question: After retraining with more Nimbus photos, what should the station do next?
options: Delete the old Cumulus photos to save space
Change the categories to Sunny, Rainy and Stormy
Test again on new photos and record the results
Assume the problem is fixed and stop checking
questions.explanation: Retraining leads back to testing — step F is a loop that continues until accuracy is good.
